# New Tashkent

New Tashkent

New district in Tashkent

**New Tashkent** is an urban development project to build a new district in [Tashkent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tashkent "Tashkent"), the capital of [Uzbekistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan "Uzbekistan"). The project is designed by Cross Works Ltd — led by architect and urban planner Hakan Ceyhan Agca — and led by the Government of Uzbekistan under the auspices of the Directorate for the Construction of the City of New Tashkent under the Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan. The Director of the Directorate and Deputy Minister of Construction is Davronjon Adilov.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-CNN2024-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-Times2025-2)

## Construction

The project plans to build a new district named **New Tashkent** or **Yangi Toshkent**, with the first phase of development, covering approximately 6,000 hectares, planned to be built by 2045.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-GovUz2025-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-Parametric2025-4) In an interview with Saidazim Sharipov - Advisor to the Director on Urban Planning Projects of the Directorate of New Tashkent, after being asked the question on how far the borders of New Tashkent would go, he responded that "the territory of New Tashkent adjoins the eastern part of the existing Tashkent. Tashkent's eastern border is defined by highway [4R12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4R12_(highway)?action=edit&redlink=1 "4R12 (highway)"). This is where the western part of New Tashkent begins. The northern border will end at the lower limits of the city of [Yangibazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangibozor,_Tashkent_Region "Yangibozor, Tashkent Region"). The eastern border runs along the [Karasu River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karasu_River "Karasu River"). In the south, the city will end roughly where Tashkent ends". When asked about the layout of New Tashkent, he responded that "Tashkent is a very unique city", therefore saying it will likely be varied rather than with a specific layout. With the question of how large an average quarter of the city will be, he responded that "different cities with different block sizes have their advantages and disadvantages. The denser the streets, the more paved areas there are. For example, in Portland, USA, blocks are 60 meters in size". When asked what would the main architectural styles in New Tashkent, he responded that "depending on the usage and function of the buildings, architectural styles will be varied".[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-5) Later, Russian sources claimed that a quarter in New Tashkent will be inspired by the Russian city of [Saint-Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Petersburg "Saint-Petersburg") and that construction of it will begin in mid 2026.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-7) It was also claimed by the management of the project that about 30% of the territory of New Tashkent will consist of parks and squares[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-8).

## Pricing and estate

As of February 10th 2026, there is no information how much estate will be constructed in New Tashkent. The Uzbekistani government claimed that on average, for 95 hectares, there will be about 15 thousands of flats. As of late 2025, about 1.8 million square meters of New Tashkent is completed. New Tashkent is positioned like a "green city" with the main goal being to preserve nature and ecology of the city. A 420 hectares large park named the Central Park will be built in New Tashkent, where about 200 thousands of trees will grow.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Tashkent#cite_note-9)
